summary: Purushottam Mahadev Joshi (1904–1989) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He worked at the University of Mumbai Library around 1935–1947 and was a Reader in Medieval History at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat (1894–1991) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Mumbai and a PhD from Harvard. He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Purushottama Bilimoria, working in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studied under Shivesh Thakur and received a PhD from La Trobe University. He held positions at Deakin University and the University of Melbourne, with visiting roles at Stony Brook and Columbia.

Pushpendra Kumar (b. 1936) is an Indologist who studied under Satya Vrat Shastri. He served as a lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi from around 1969 to 2001 and as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University.
Puthezhethu Rama Menon (1891–1973) was active in Indology. He served as a judge on the Chief Court of Cochin and was president of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at King's College London by 2014 and later served there as a postdoctoral research fellow (attested 2017).

Pál Büchler (1877–1946) was an Indology scholar who earned his PhD from Eötvös Loránd University, where he studied from around 1897 to 1907. He later served as a professor at the Commercial School in Târgu-Mureș (1926–1930).

Péter-Dániel Szántó works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford, under Alexis Sanderson and Mária Négyesi. He held posts at Merton College, All Souls College, Leiden, and ELTE.
Qian Cao is a scholar of Indology and philosophy affiliated with Ghent University, where she is attested in 2026 as both a PhD student and faculty member.

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington, where she earned a PhD under Collett Cox. She is attested at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2026.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Supervised by Hung Wu and Irene Winter, he studied at the University of Warwick and UCAS. He taught at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and researched at Dunhuang Academy.

Qichao Liang (1873–1929) worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Youwei Kang, he headed the Translation Bureau, was chief lecturer at Current Affairs Academy, taught at Nankai and Tsinghua, and directed the National Library of China.

Qing Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ronald Eric Emmerick, later heading a department at Peking University (ca. 1987–2022).

Qingying Chen (1942–2022) was a Tibetologist and historian. He studied at Qinghai University for Nationalities and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He taught at Delingha High School and Qinghai Nationalities University before joining the China Tibetology Research Center.

Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Northwest Normal University, Central China Normal University, and Sichuan University, and held professorships at Peking University (1998–2014) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

Quentin Devers is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He worked as a research assistant at the University of Virginia (2008–2010), an archaeologist at Heritage WA (2012), and joined the CNRS as chargé de recherche in 2016.
R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras from around 1980 to 1990.

R. D. Vadekar (1902–1986) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar and served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).
